units.title: At the wet doorway
units.alignmentNote: Complete set of five short communicative-response choices; limited extra context is an explicit provisional adaptation, not independent age calibration.

materials.title: At the wet doorway
materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Child: My umbrella is dripping. Where can I put it?
Teacher: ____

2. Teacher: Are your socks wet too?
Child: ____

3. Child: I cannot close this umbrella.
Friend: ____

4. Teacher: Please wipe your shoes on the mat.
Child: ____

5. Child: Is the rain stopping?
Teacher: ____

questions.prompt:
Child: My umbrella is dripping. Where can I put it?
Teacher: ____
options: In this bucket by the door.
questions.explanation: The bucket is a place for a wet umbrella. Time, a name and a birthday do not answer where to put it.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Are your socks wet too?
Child: ____
options: No. Only my shoes are wet.
questions.explanation: The reply directly denies wet socks and identifies wet shoes. A location, a food request and another child’s class do not answer this condition question.

questions.prompt:
Child: I cannot close this umbrella.
Friend: ____
questions.explanation: Let me try offers help with the difficult umbrella. Colour description, age and identifying birds do not help.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Please wipe your shoes on the mat.
Child: ____
questions.explanation: Agreeing and checking the action responds to the instruction. The other statements do not concern cleaning shoes.

questions.prompt:
Child: Is the rain stopping?
Teacher: ____
options: Yes. We can see the sun now.
questions.explanation: Yes with the sun appearing answers the weather change. Naming possessions, preference and a person’s location do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: Is anyone sitting here?
Friend: ____
options: No. You can sit next to me.
questions.explanation: The reply confirms the seat is available and invites sitting. Possessions, time and a parent’s job do not answer seat availability.

questions.prompt:
Child: I have dropped my spoon.
Teacher: ____
questions.explanation: A clean replacement spoon addresses the dropped utensil. Cat state, weather and age do not.

questions.prompt:
Friend: Would you like more rice?
Child: ____
options: No, thank you. I have enough.
questions.explanation: Declining politely and saying enough answers the offer. Location, shoes and ability are unrelated.

questions.prompt:
Child: This soup is very hot.
Teacher: ____
options: It is a nice blue bag.
Wait a little before you eat it.
questions.explanation: Waiting allows hot soup to cool. A bag description, family count and a hobby do not address temperature.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Where do the empty cups go?
Child: ____
questions.explanation: The tray is the requested place for cups. Feeling, day and family identity do not answer where.

materials.title: Before the birthday party
materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Dad: We need one chair for each child. Are there enough?
Child: ____

2. Child: Where shall I put the birthday card?
Mum: ____

3. Friend: May I help with the party?
Child: ____

4. Mum: Who is the cake for?
Child: ____

5. Child: The candles are ready. Shall we call everyone?
Dad: ____

questions.prompt:
Dad: We need one chair for each child. Are there enough?
Child: ____
questions.explanation: The reply states a shortage and needed chairs. Cake colour, a song preference and location do not answer whether seating is enough.

questions.prompt:
Child: Where shall I put the birthday card?
Mum: ____
questions.explanation: Beside the present gives the place for the card. Ability, day and duck count do not.

questions.prompt:
Friend: May I help with the party?
Child: ____
options: Yes. Please put these cups on the table.
questions.explanation: Giving a useful task accepts the offer of help. Age, door colour and pet ownership do not.

questions.prompt:
Mum: Who is the cake for?
Child: ____
options: For my brother. It is his birthday.
questions.explanation: For my brother identifies the recipient. Size, location and ability do not answer for whom.

questions.prompt:
Child: The candles are ready. Shall we call everyone?
Dad: ____
options: Yes. Ask them to come in.
questions.explanation: Calling guests in accepts the suggestion. Other replies do not concern gathering people.

materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Child: May I sit by the window?
Dad: ____

2. Child: Is this our stop?
Dad: ____

3. Dad: The bus is moving. Please hold on.
Child: ____

4. Child: That lady has no seat.
Dad: ____

5. Driver: Please take your bag when you leave.
Child: ____

questions.prompt:
Child: May I sit by the window?
Dad: ____
options: Yes. I will sit beside you.
questions.explanation: Permission and Dad’s seat plan directly answer the request. Location, job and coat colour do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: Is this our stop?
Dad: ____
options: Not yet. We get off at the next one.
questions.explanation: The reply identifies the correct stop as the next one. Flower description, body count and swimming ability do not.

questions.prompt:
Dad: The bus is moving. Please hold on.
Child: ____
options: All right. I have the rail.
questions.explanation: Holding the rail follows the safety instruction. Introduction, weather and identity do not confirm holding on.

questions.prompt:
Child: That lady has no seat.
Dad: ____
questions.explanation: Offering the child’s seat addresses the standing passenger. Time, food preference and bike ownership do not.

questions.prompt:
Driver: Please take your bag when you leave.
Child: ____
questions.explanation: Thanks acknowledges the reminder to take a bag. Age, window state and bird observation do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: My toy train does not move. Can you look at it?
Dad: ____
questions.explanation: Asking the child to bring it accepts the inspection request. Day, shoe colour and identity do not.

questions.prompt:
Dad: Where is the train’s battery?
Child: ____
questions.explanation: The box location answers where the battery is. Time, preference and height do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: Do we need a new battery?
Dad: ____
options: Yes. This one has no power.
questions.explanation: A powerless battery gives the reason for replacement. Singing, an unrelated location and hunger do not answer the need.

questions.prompt:
Dad: Please give me the small screwdriver.
Child: ____
questions.explanation: Checking which small tool to hand over responds to the request. Bird count, bag colour and weather do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: It works now! Thank you, Dad.
Dad: ____
questions.explanation: You’re welcome answers thanks and Have fun suits the repaired toy. Other statements do not respond to gratitude.

materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Child: Can I use this paper to cover my book?

questions.prompt:
Child: Can I use this paper to cover my book?
Teacher: ____
options: Yes. There is enough for you.
questions.explanation: Permission with enough paper answers the request. Pet ownership, time and ability do not.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Which book needs a cover?
Child: ____
options: The storybook with the torn cover.
questions.explanation: Naming the damaged storybook selects the book. Weather, health and another group’s location do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: I cannot keep the paper flat.
Teacher: ____
options: Put this heavy book on it.
questions.explanation: A heavy book holds paper flat. Taste, family identity and thirst do not solve the problem.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Do you want to draw on the new cover?
Child: ____
options: Yes. I will draw a little house.
questions.explanation: The child accepts and states a drawing plan. Location, age and sport ability do not answer the offer.

questions.prompt:
Child: My name is very small. Can you read it?
Teacher: ____
options: Not very well. Please write it bigger.
questions.explanation: The reply addresses readability and suggests larger writing. Lunch identity, possessions and weekday do not.
